name: Pedestrian Fine-Grained Classification Benchmark
description: A video dataset that is designed to study fine-grained categorisation of pedestrians is introduced. Pedestrians were recorded "in-the-wild" from a moving vehicle. Annotations include bounding boxes, tracks, 14 keypoints with occlusion information and the fine-grained categories of age (5 classes), sex (2 classes), weight (3 classes) and clothing style (4 classes). There are a total of 27,454 bounding box and pose labels across 4222 tracks. This dataset is designed to train and test algorithms for fine-grained categorisation of people, it is also useful for benchmarking tracking, detection and pose estimation of pedestrians. State-of-the-art algorithms for fine-grained classification and pose estimation were tested using the dataset and the results are reported as a useful performance baseline.
reputation: A niche but useful academic benchmark for pedestrian fine-grained recognition and related vision tasks, mainly cited in research on detection, tracking, and pose estimation rather than broad leaderboard use.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark with a relatively small dataset; results are often reported across multiple subtasks, and direct cross-paper comparison can be difficult.
